Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-02
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Kline (Redwood AE), Jordan Park (Redwood SE), Sofia Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Emma Torres (Atlas Head of Platform), Liam O'Neill (Atlas SRE), Priya Raman (Atlas Security), Derek Ho (Atlas Product)

Summary (auto): quick alignment on post-incident responsibilities, scope of fallback runbook, evidence needed for SOC2 audit, and next steps for latency benchmarks and pilot guardrails.

Topics: incident recap, ownership matrix, fallback routing, KV cache invalidation strategy, private deployment vs dedicated, compliance packet, benchmark plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanna make sure today's tight — we set expectations, outcomes: runbook alignment and clear owners.
[00:12] Emma (Atlas): yeah thanks, we've had a couple of late-night pages last week so, um, want to make sure handoffs are sharp, and that the fallback actually runs and doesn't cascade.
[00:22] Jordan (SE): quick recap from Redwood side: root cause looked like a KV cache invalidation race during burst, combined with a misrouted fallback that hit a lower-tier model with different tokenization, so tokens spiked and then autoscaler reacted late. apologies for noise.
[00:40] Liam (Atlas): that's consistent with our logs, the cache flush was noisy — we saw request 503s and then 504s, then a surge into the fallback path — it amplified.
[00:51] Priya (Atlas): security perspective: we need to see audit trails for the fallback decision and confirmation that fallback data doesn't get persisted in the wrong residency. our compliance team will ask.
[01:03] Maya (AE): totally. Jordan and I sketched a runbook — high-level steps, who calls who, automatic thresholds — we'll share. but we want Atlas to confirm on thresholds and who owns the manual rollback.
[01:18] Derek (Product): quick Q: will fallback routing always go to a hosted model? we prefer dedicated for certain flows but we don't want added latency.
[01:28] Jordan (SE): short answer: routing can be policy-defined. you can prefer dedicated pools or hosted variants by traffic tag or route. the tradeoff is cost and sometimes cold-start latency on dedicated after scale-down.
[01:44] Emma (Atlas): are there proven SLO numbers for fallback to dedicated? last incident, the fallback seemed slower than primary and caused a bad customer experience.
[01:54] Jordan (SE): we have perf profiles per model and region — I'll attach the perf sheet but in practice fallback to a smaller-quantized variant can be faster than cold dedicated pools. it's workload dependent, e.g., short single-turn calls vs long chat sessions.
[02:10] Maya (AE): uh-huh and we can show you the telemetry from the incident — token timings, queue lengths. Maya: we'll also show the KV cache TTLs that were in play.
[02:22] Emma (Atlas): good. Priya, on compliance, what do you need from us?
[02:27] Priya (Atlas): SOC2 packet, encryption at rest details (KMS), audit logs for fallback routing decisions, retention policy for prompt/response. residency — we can't send PII outside EU.
[02:38] Sofia (CSM): Redwood supports customer-managed KMS in Private deployments and can restrict region. we have an enterprise packet; I'll send the link.
[02:47] Emma (Atlas): great — send it. also we need a clear ownership matrix — who executes the runbook steps during an incident.
[02:55] Jordan (SE): proposed owners: Atlas SREs for mitigating their upstream load; Redwood SE for runtime toggles and model routing; Redwood AE/CSM for escalation comms. specific items like replaying traffic and KV cache invalidation scripts we can provide.
[03:12] Liam (Atlas): replaying traffic — can you give us a config? we run it against a staging cluster, but we need to be sure it's representative.
[03:20] Jordan (SE): yes, we'll produce a traffic replay config and a smaller subset of production traces that are safe, scrubbed. note: replay can be tricky if timestamps are strict, so we'll include guidance.
[03:32] Derek (Atlas): pricing concern: if we force a dedicated pool as fallback, cost could spike. we need a cost guardrail.
[03:40] Maya (AE): understood — we can include cost ceilings in the runbook and an automatic fallback to a cheaper hosted quantized variant if spend exceeds threshold. we'll lay out the three-tier policy.
[03:52] Emma (Atlas): micro question: during the incident we saw a bunch of 502s labelled as "model mismatch" in Redwood logs — is that the tokenization issue you mentioned?
[04:01] Jordan (SE): yes there was a mismatch between the model tokenizer used by the customer preprocessor and the hot fallback. some tokens got cut, leading to longer decode loops. it's subtle and depends on model family.
[04:13] Priya (Atlas): can you ensure fallback models keep the same tokenizer families? we can't have unexpected behavior for customer-facing text.
[04:20] Jordan (SE): policy can pin tokenizer families to avoid that. we'll add a rule in the routing matrix.
[04:27] Maya (AE): action note: include a tokenizer compatibility check as step 2 in the runbook.
[04:33] Emma (Atlas): thanks. also the KV cache TTL — what was it set to? we need recommended TTLs by workload.
[04:39] Jordan (SE): we recommended conservative TTLs before; during spike someone shortened TTLs to free memory which triggered mass invalidation. recommended: staggered TTLs and jittered invalidation windows. we'll send config.
[04:52] Liam (Atlas): for the record, we also saw autoscaler spike slow because our cluster scale policy took 4m to add nodes. can Redwood recommend pod sizes / burst settings?
[05:02] Jordan (SE): yes, we can share autoscaler best practices — and we can test a pre-warm strategy to keep a small buffer of warm GPUs for critical routes.
[05:12] Sofia (CSM): note: pre-warm is part of Dedicated offering, customers can set pre-warm capacity to avoid cold starts.
[05:20] Derek (Atlas): is there a simple matrix we can get that maps incident types to runbook playbooks? like TTL invalidation -> step list A, tokenizer mismatch -> step list B.
[05:29] Maya (AE): yes, that's exactly what we'll deliver. we'll produce a one-pager mapping the top 6 incident archetypes to clear steps and owners.
[05:38] Emma (Atlas): perfect. on evidence — Priya wants audit entries for fallback decisions — can Redwood correlate a fallback event to the specific request IDs?
[05:47] Jordan (SE): yes, request-level trace ids are preserved across routing hops; we log decision reasons in trace metadata. we'll demonstrate with a sample trace (redacted).
[05:57] Priya (Atlas): retention — we need to know how long traces are kept and whether we can export them to our SIEM.
[06:04] Sofia (CSM): we have export hooks; we can set retention windows per account, and exports to S3 or your SIEM via secure connectors. I'll include the docs link.
[06:13] Emma (Atlas): good. okay let's get tactical — what are the first three deliverables and owners?
[06:19] Maya (AE): 1) Redwood: updated fallback runbook draft (Maya/Jordan) 2) Redwood: traffic replay config and guidance (Jordan) 3) Atlas: run the latency benchmark and share results (Emma/Liam)
[06:30] Derek (Atlas): timeline?
[06:32] Maya (AE): aim to have drafts by Friday — 2026-09-06. benchmarks back by 2026-09-10. security Qs by 2026-09-04.
[06:40] Liam (Atlas): ok that works.
[06:42] Emma (Atlas): one more thing — could we schedule a dry-run of the runbook next week? like an incident simulation?
[06:49] Jordan (SE): yes, we do tabletop drills. we can do a 60-minute sim: run through triggers, toggles, comms. we'll schedule for the week of 2026-09-13 if that fits.
[06:59] Maya (AE): great. anyone object?
[07:02] Priya (Atlas): no, sounds good. also, Redwood — please confirm that Private deployment option supports our KMS key wrapping and EU-only egress before we do the dry-run.
[07:14] Sofia (CSM): noted - we'll attach a Private deployment checklist.
[07:19] Derek (Atlas): on cost again, Maya, can you send a simple cost model for pre-warm + fallback tiers? we need CFO approval for extra buffers.
[07:28] Maya (AE): will do, short spreadsheet with scenarios.
[07:31] (brief cross-talk)
[07:38] Emma (Atlas): ok cool. I want to call out that our users were hit for about 7 minutes of poor responses; that's the executive story so we'll need a clear mitigation timeline.
[07:47] Maya (AE): understood — we'll include an exec summary in the runbook email.
[07:51] Jordan (SE): technical note: we'll include a quick script to validate tokenizer families across model variants to avoid mismatches.
[07:58] Liam (Atlas): nice. good to see concrete items.
[08:03] Maya (AE): recap and next steps: Redwood to send runbook draft, traffic replay config, perf sheet, and SOC2/ISO packet links. Atlas to run benchmarks and confirm owners for manual rollback. Schedule tabletop for week of 9/13.
[08:20] Emma (Atlas): yes. thanks everyone.
[08:23] Maya (AE): thanks all. we'll follow up with notes and links.
